newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech bank governor says money supply on target. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech bank governor says money supply on target. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]

text.p: Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky on Wednesday said the key M2 money supply measure is now in the central bank's target range.

Tosovsky expects expansion of M2, which was 13.2 percent (corrects from 15.7 percent) year-on-year in August, excluding funds from the sale of a stake in SPT Telecom, will slow further in the coming months.
"We have signals that the decline in the dynamics in the money supply growth should continue in the following months," Tosovsky told a forum of business leaders in Prague.

He said the central bank's target range was between 13-17 percent, though he did not say if this was including funds from the $1.32 billion sale of state shares in SPT Telecom, the country's main telephone operator, to a Swiss-Dutch consortium.

With the SPT funds, M2, which measures currency, demand deposits, time and savings deposits, and foreign currency deposits, was 15.7 percent in August. In July, M2 stood at 17.1 percent without SPT funds, and at 17.6 percent with the money.
Tosovsky added that he expects the M2 figure to be at the lower end of the range "by the end of the year".
The central bank governor also re-iterated that his top priority was still lowering inflation.
He said this will help exporters by reducing pressure on the crown because interest rates will be able to come down, thus reducing the interest rate differential with other countries.
Year-on-year inflation stood at 8.9 percent in September.
